purpose: Correct the main hero image following user feedback about a missing door and implausible fitting action.
rejected_first_revision: The first edit removed tools but showed the door separated from the body. It was rejected and never committed to the website.
prompt:
Edit the first supplied image to correct ONE serious physical error: the open driver's door is currently floating, detached from the right-hand-drive car across the gap occupied by people. Make it a physically real attached door. Preserve the original BMW dashboard/steering wheel/Jeff Gosling grip and bent black lever (second supplied photo locks this hardware), navy-clad technician identities, bright workshop and calm visual-inspection theme.

CRITICAL GEOMETRY: The door's leading/front hinged edge must meet the existing car-body A-pillar at the right edge of the dashboard directly, with visible upper and lower short metal hinges connecting the two, no gap between disconnected door and body. The door swings OUTWARD from that attachment and extends diagonally into the right foreground. Its large inner door card, armrest, handle, window frame and side mirror remain visible. Put the attached door in the foreground between camera and people; its lower solid panel MUST correctly occlude the technicians' lower bodies. This correct occlusion is important. Nobody stands between door's front hinged edge and the car's A-pillar. The technicians have moved farther OUTSIDE the car behind the opened door, now standing upright and gently leaning to LOOK through the open window/doorway at the controls. Heads and shoulders can appear above the low window sill (window rolled fully down); lower bodies mostly hidden by the real door panel. Hands rest naturally on their own sides or loosely at waist, away from controls. Do not simply retain the crouching people in the hinge gap. Recompose camera and enlarge framing if needed to make coherent car anatomy.

NO tool, torch, screwdriver, hex key, fastening, touch on dashboard, drilling, installation or pointing into panels. They are only visually reviewing a fully fitted control. Maintain physically connected sill and pillars, realistic human anatomy, same unchanged hand-control hardware. Do not draw a huge bridge bracket between detached door and body. Door is connected by two normal short hinges right beside the dashboard, not across a person's width. Real automotive workshop photograph, not a cutaway car. Landscape around 16:9, no overlaid text/logos/watermark. Give the attachment, door and controls room inside the edges. Verify hinge connection and foreground occlusion before finalizing.
review: The chosen image shows the solid open door connected beside the dashboard, short visible hinges, window/mirror details and technicians behind the door looking at the finished control. No tools, fastening action or hands on the dashboard are visible. This is AI campaign imagery rather than a photograph of actual staff or installation work.
